input.question: Who takes over essential jobs during a strike?
input.ground_truth: If you are referring to essential services such as police, firemen, emergency rescue etc, in many jurisdictions it is actually illegal for them to strike. For example in New York State the Public Employees Fair Employment Act has banned all public employees from striking since 1967, and in the UK the 1919 Police Act bans all police from going on strike. In exchange, many of these laws have a binding arbitration clause in case of an impasse in labor negotiations.

First, what's a strike? Well, a strike is when workers stop doing their jobs to protest or demand better conditions. But some jobs are really important, like keeping hospitals running or making sure we have food. So, during a strike, those essential jobs can't stop.

Now, who takes over these jobs? Well, not everyone can stop working. Some people have to keep working to make sure everything is okay. For example, doctors and nurses can't stop because people are sick and need help. Similarly, people who work in grocery stores keep selling food so we don't run out. 

So, the answer is that even when some workers go on strike, others keep working to make sure essential services are provided. It's like when some kids are playing and others are taking care of the toys so everything stays in order.
